newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BEKAERT HIT BY DUPONT KEVLAR TYRE.
newsitem.headline: BEKAERT HIT BY DUPONT KEVLAR TYRE.

text.p: Shares in Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert fell sharply on Tuesday after news that U.S. chemical giant maker Dupont had developed a fibre that replaces steel cord in tyres and reduces their weight.
"The market is definitely overreacting to Dupont's advertisement in the Economist this weekend," Bekaert's vice- president Willy Snaet told Reuters.
"The Kevlar tyre is 20 percent more expensive than normal tyres," he said, adding that in the short to medium term it was not a threat.
Snaet said Bekaert got a report every two years from the Stanford Research Instutite (SRI) on Kevlar development and the conclusion was it was less of a threat now than 10 years ago.
Berkaert produces steel cord tyre reinforcement and controls 22 percent of the world market, according to a report by Investext Broker's Report in July 1996.
Dupont's advertisement in the Economist said the new Kevlar-reinforced tyre would reduce overall weight by 30 percent and in turn cut fuel consumption.
The new Kevlar tyre, called ULW, produced by Dunlop has been installed on the new Audi A3 cars.
"The actual prices that Kevlar is sold to the tyre industry is too low to justify expansion investments, so the tendency is for the price of Kevlar to go up," Snaet said.
He said the quality of Steel cord had increased tremendously while the price had fallen.
General Bank steel analyst Sandra Vandersmissen said the new product had many advantages but that it was too expensive.
"To produce Kevlar would not necessarily be economically viable at the moment as one would have to set up new factories because of its completely new technology," she added.
But she said "the product looks more promising in the long term".
Dealers said the market was overreacting to the Dupont news but expected the price to recover.
"We are thinking of changing our recommendation to hold from sell," Vandersmissen said.

But she added that Bekaert was too expensive on price earnings levels especially if one looked at the steel cord business which was not doing very well and this could also have reflected in Tuesday's selling.
Bekaert fell over 7 percent in early trading but recovered somewhat at 1415 GMT to fall 4.61 percent to 23,800 francs, after closing on Monday at 24,950 francs.
